🚨 *new alert — needs human* (score: 9)
Channel: alert-system (DD-sourced this cycle — no Slack MCP; see note)  •  bug-type guess: env  •  alerts in group: 64
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (ms-authentication-api, ms-tables-fields-api per ownership.md — note ms-tables-fields-api's DD monitor tag says `team:runtime`, ownership.md is authoritative); several affected services (`ms-documents-api`, `ms-tags-api`, `miurl-agent`, `eda_orchestrator_api`, `designer-core-api`) are `unmapped` in ownership.md

Symptoms:
  - ms-authentication-api and ms-tables-fields-api each show a genuine multi-hour zero-traffic/zero-log gap, independently confirmed in BOTH Datadog APM metrics and Elasticsearch logs (auth-api: ~3.5h, 2026-07-05 01:06-04:36 UTC; tables-fields: ~2h, 02:00-04:00 UTC), followed by a burst of activity as each recovers
  - 51 other Datadog monitors across 6 different team tags (admin/vae/first-strike/devops/runtime/poiesis) fired "no-traffic / 5xx elevated / P95 latency high" within roughly the same ~45-minute window (04:36-05:20 UTC), plus a smaller ~1h secondary recurrence on ms-account-api ~07:00-08:00 UTC
  - Gateway and runtime-core-api (hosted separately) show continuous, ungapped traffic throughout — this looks scoped to the `microservices.methodlocal.int`-hosted tier, not a whole-stack outage
  - Zero corroborating application errors found anywhere checked (gateway, ms-authentication-api, ms-account-api, tables-fields, eda_consumer, ms-scheduler-api all returned 0 status:error hits) — a silent availability/telemetry gap, not an error-throwing incident
  - Per CLAUDE.md, existing sessions likely kept working via cached JWTs (Redis) throughout — only new sessions/token refresh would have been affected

Trace IDs: n/a (availability gap, not an error signature — no representative trace/request id to cite)
Likely cause: `microservices.methodlocal.int`-hosted tier (or its host/VM) unreachable or degraded for ~3.5h overnight (2026-07-05 ~01:06-04:36 UTC, shorter ~1h recurrence ~07:00-08:00 UTC), silencing both DD APM and ES/Logstash telemetry for the services it hosts. Could not confirm via deploy correlation (methodcrm-org git access 403'd, known token gap) or via host/SSH-level checks (out of scope for this cycle's tools). A maintenance/patching window is plausible given the timing and clean self-recovery.
Suggested next action: page infra/DevOps to check AWS/host console + IIS logs for the `microservices.methodlocal.int` target group around 2026-07-05 01:00-04:40 UTC and 07:00-08:00 UTC; confirm whether this was a planned maintenance window

🚨 *new alert — needs human* (score: 7)

Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Transactions`

Symptoms:
  - DD monitor 295928665 ([Rainforest] Outbound API P95 Latency > 3s, service:runtime-core-api, integration:rainforest) currently in Alert state
  - Peak p95 latency 7.16s vs the 3s threshold (ratio ≈1.4x) at 2026-07-05T08:19:00Z, for calls to peer.hostname api.rainforestpay.com
  - Metric data stops entirely after ~08:36Z (no further calls to Rainforest observed through 11:10Z) — consistent with a low-volume, on-demand integration rather than an ongoing issue
  - No corroborating application errors found on runtime-core-api in the same window

Trace IDs: n/a (not pulled to trace level this cycle — time budget; see APM traces link below to drill in)
Likely cause: Third-party latency/degradation on Rainforest's side during a ~15-20 minute window (08:19-08:36Z), self-recovering. No Method-side deploy correlation available (methodcrm-org git 403'd, known gap) and no corroborating errors found.
Suggested next action: monitor for recurrence; if it recurs, escalate to Transactions team and consider adding #alert-transactions to the routine's polled channels (currently only caught via full DD monitor scan)
